false_positives.candidate:
Legacy membership PATCH requests now silently change visibility

The resources route still sends PATCH requests to update, but the incremental membership handler has been removed. For a visible group, PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes: {delete: "alice"} now ignores the requested removal, sets visible to false because that parameter is absent, and returns success. Existing callers can believe membership was revoked when it remains intact. Preserve the supported PATCH behavior or explicitly reject legacy payloads instead of silently applying an unrelated update.

Public member lists are truncated without pagination

This action now limits every group to 50 members, but the public group-members route calls findMembers only once and its template has no pagination or further loading. Nonautomatic groups with more than 50 members therefore lose the remainder of their public member list, whereas previously all members were returned. Add public pagination or incremental loading alongside the endpoint change.

Capture the group before opening the removal confirmation

The confirmation message names the current group, but its callback retrieves the controller's model again. If the administrator navigates to another group while the Bootbox dialog remains open, such as through browser Back, confirming removes the user from the newly selected group rather than the group named in the dialog. Capture the original group before opening the confirmation and invoke removeMember on that captured model.

Membership reloads use an unsaved editable group name

Both membership mutations reload through findMembers, which addresses the group by model.name. The admin name field changes that property immediately, before Save persists the rename. If an administrator edits the name and then adds or removes a member, the mutation succeeds using the group ID, but the reload requests the nonexistent new name and fails, leaving the displayed membership stale. Reload using a persisted identifier or persisted name.

Reset pending usernames when switching groups

The admin-group controller is reused across group routes, and usernames is now standalone controller state. setupController changes only the model, while addMembers also leaves usernames populated after success. Users selected or added in group A consequently remain selected after navigating to group B and are included in its next Add request, potentially granting unintended membership. Clear the selection when changing groups and after a successful addition.

Ignore stale member-page responses

Next and Previous update the offset immediately and allow another request before the first finishes, while every findMembers response unconditionally overwrites members and offset. Clicking Next twice can request offsets 50 and 100; if the offset-100 response arrives first, the later offset-50 response moves the display back to the earlier page. Serialize pagination requests or track request order so an older response cannot overwrite the latest navigation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update match statistics atomically

The method reads match_count, increments it in Ruby, and saves it without locking the row. Concurrent checks for the same address can both read the same count and overwrite each other with the same incremented value, losing matches. An older request can also overwrite a newer last_match_at value. Use an atomic database update or a row lock to preserve these statistics.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same core bug: should_block_email? performs a non-atomic statistics update as a side effect of a read/check, creating race conditions where concurrent requests can lose match counts or overwrite last_match_at. The candidate's focus on atomic updates addresses the concurrency concern raised in the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
Normalize email addresses before storing and matching blocklist entries

The lookup uses case-sensitive equality, and BlockedEmail does not normalize addresses when storing them or checking them. An entry for `blocked@example.com` therefore does not match `blocked@EXAMPLE.COM`, although domain casing does not change the mailbox. The signup flow assigns the submitted email directly, allowing a blocked user to bypass this restriction by changing the domain's casing. Apply consistent email canonicalization to both stored entries and lookup values.

Require a nonempty email-error array before rejecting an address

EmailValidator reads `record.errors[:email]` even when the email passes validation, which creates an empty array in ActiveModel::Errors. The controller's `errors.to_hash` consequently includes `email: []` when signup fails for another field. Empty arrays are truthy in JavaScript, so this condition caches the valid address as rejected—for example, after a username becomes unavailable between the availability check and submission. Correcting the username then leaves submission disabled until the email changes or the page reloads. Check that the email-error array contains an error before caching the address.

Blocked-match statistics are rolled back by failed user saves

Calling the mutating should_block? method during User validation makes its statistics update part of the surrounding User#save transaction. When the address is blocked, this validator adds an error and the user save rolls back, undoing BlockedEmail's match_count and last_match_at updates too. Paths that call save directly, such as User.create_for_email, therefore reject the address without recording the match. Persist match tracking outside the failing user-save transaction and cover a blocked User#save in an integration test.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve panel right alignment in the legacy box fallback

The new flexbox mixin emits `display: -webkit-box` and `display: -moz-box`, but those legacy box layouts do not distribute free space to `margin-left: auto` as modern flexbox does. In browsers using that fallback, such as Safari 6, removing `float: right` leaves the header panel immediately after the logo/topic information instead of against the right edge. The legacy-box path needs its own space-distribution rule to preserve the navigation layout.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same layout regression: removing float:right and relying on flexbox margin-left:auto fails to keep the header panel right-aligned in non-modern flex contexts. The candidate's legacy box fallback framing is a semantic match for the golden comment's concern.

false_positives.candidate:
Emit the alignment property for the Mozilla box fallback

Both display mixins emit Mozilla's legacy box layout (`-moz-box` or `-moz-inline-box`), but `align-items()` never emits `-moz-box-align`. Neither standard `align-items` nor the WebKit-prefixed properties control that layout. Firefox versions selecting this fallback therefore ignore the requested centering of header and small-action content and the baseline alignment of bullet badges. This is especially visible for small actions because their previous vertical padding is removed in this change. Add the matching Mozilla alignment declaration.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
Apply the website visibility restriction to website_name

Unlike `website`, `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. For anonymous views of restricted TL0 users, `website` is omitted but the new field still exposes its host and, for matching domains, its path. The template also displays this value even when `website` is absent. Gate the derived field with the same restriction. The added `include_website_name` method lacks the required `?` suffix and is not a serializer inclusion hook.

Keep the website label synchronized after preference edits

`website_name` is now a plain server-provided value rather than a computed property observing `model.website`. However, `User.save()` submits website changes and only applies `bio_excerpt` from the response; it never refreshes `website_name`. Until user details are reloaded, adding a website can leave it invisible, changing one can display the old site's label with the new href, and removing one can leave the old label visible. Update the derived value when saving or retain a reactive calculation.

Compare hostnames case-insensitively

Ruby's `URI(...).host` preserves hostname case, but the equality and suffix comparisons here are case-sensitive. For an instance at `example.com`, a valid website such as `https://EXAMPLE.COM/user` therefore displays only `EXAMPLE.COM`, despite referring to the same domain. Normalize both hostnames for comparison so these URLs receive the complete path too.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Compare message origins exactly rather than by substring

The substring check accepts origins that merely prefix the configured forum origin. For example, with `discourseUrl` set to `https://forum.example.com/`, a message from `https://forum.example.co` passes this check. An unrelated frame or window with a reference to the embedding page can then send trusted resize messages and manipulate the comments frame's height. Compare against the parsed origin exactly and verify that the message source is this iframe.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same origin-validation bypass: a substring/indexOf check can accept a malicious or merely similar origin instead of requiring an exact origin match. The candidate's example differs, but the underlying bug and security concern are the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve HTML sanitization for raw-HTML posts

Returning `raw` bypasses HTML sanitization on both creation and subsequent edits. PollFeed passes external feed HTML into TopicEmbed.import without sanitizing it, and Nokogiri fragment parsing does not remove scripts or event handlers. TopicEmbed also appends an attribution link containing an unescaped embed URL after Readability filtering. These values reach `post.cooked` and are rendered with `raw`, allowing stored JavaScript to execute on the forum origin. Skipping Markdown rendering must not skip HTML safety checks.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same TopicEmbed.import XSS concern: an attribution link with an unescaped embed URL reaches rendered HTML. It does not mention the nil/NoMethodError case, but the core vulnerability matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fix the invalid ERB conditional terminator

The template closes its conditional with `end if`, leaving a trailing `if` without a condition. This produces invalid Ruby when Rails compiles the ERB template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. The terminator should be `end`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the invalid ERB terminator `end if` and state it should be `end` to avoid a template syntax error.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Support RSS bodies outside the Atom content field

Valid RSS feeds commonly store item bodies in `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries can provide only `summary`. Those entries have no `i.content`, so calling `.scrub` here raises instead of importing them and aborts the rest of the polling run. Select the available body field and handle entries without a body; tests should exercise actual RSS and Atom fixtures rather than only the execute guards.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: calling scrub on i.content assumes content is present, but valid RSS/Atom entries may only have description/content:encoded/summary, causing a nil error and aborting polling. The candidate proposes selecting an available field and handling missing bodies, matching the golden fallback concern.

false_positives.candidate:
Validate redirect destinations before fetching remote content

TopicRetriever checks only the initial URL's host, while open-uri follows redirects here without rechecking the destination. An anonymous embed request pointing to a redirect on the allowed host can therefore make the worker fetch a non-allowlisted host or an internal HTTP resource, whose content may then be imported into a public topic. Validate the scheme and destination of every redirect rather than treating the initial host check as sufficient.

Resolve relative URLs against the complete article URL

This conversion treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as local paths, producing a broken URL such as `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. It also leaves path-relative references such as `images/photo.jpg` and `../other-article` unchanged, so browsers resolve them against the Discourse page rather than the source article. The same problems affect images below. Use URI resolution against the complete article URL for both href and src.

Defer post jobs until the outer import transaction commits

PostCreator.create enqueues processing and featured-user jobs after its own Post.transaction block, but that transaction joins the outer Topic.transaction opened here. Consequently, those jobs are enqueued before the post and topic are committed, and before the TopicEmbed insertion can fail. Another worker can process rows that are not yet visible, or work for an import that subsequently rolls back. Arrange for these jobs and publication side effects to run only after the outer transaction commits.

Update imported content and its hash under one lock

The post revision and content_sha1 update are separate operations without a transaction or row lock. Scheduled polling and retrieval-triggered polling can overlap: one import can save body A, another save body B and hash B, then the first write hash A. The stored hash then describes different content from the post, and a subsequent import of A skips a necessary revision because the hashes match. Serialize updates for an embed and commit its post revision and hash together.

Set the retrieval throttle and its expiration atomically

SETNX and EXPIRE are separate commands. If the worker terminates between them, the retrieval key remains without an expiration. Every later non-staff attempt then sees SETNX fail and refuses to retrieve that URL indefinitely, leaving the embed stuck on the reloading screen. Use an atomic Redis operation that sets the key only when absent and assigns its TTL in the same command.

Preserve historical topic timestamps during Disqus imports

The previous topic creation passed the exported thread's `created_at`, but TopicEmbed.import_remote has no creation-time option and creates the first post at the current time. Replies still receive their historical timestamps. Importing an old export therefore makes every topic appear newly created and gives its first post a timestamp later than its replies, corrupting discussion history and chronological statistics. Pass the exported creation time through the new import path.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve the existing width/height downsize API

Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition. Existing four-argument calls now treat the numeric height as `opts` and fail when `optimize` accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`; five-argument calls raise `ArgumentError`. Support both argument forms within one definition rather than silently removing the existing API.
true_positives.reasoning: The content matches the golden comment: both describe the second `downsize` definition overriding the first because Ruby does not overload by arity, breaking existing width/height callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Keep attachment validation tied to its configured size limit

The hardcoded 10 MB limit also applies to attachments, although the controller only downsizes images. Attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and are uploaded unchanged, while attachments permitted by a configured limit above 10 MB are now blocked. Relax the image limit without replacing the configured attachment limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: a hardcoded 10 MB client-side limit replaces the configured per-type size settings (e.g. max_attachment_size_kb), causing client validation to diverge from the server and incorrectly allow or block attachments.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use supported resize dimensions for the animated GIF branch

When the input path does end in `.gif` and animation is enabled, this percentage-based call reaches `resize_instructions_animated`, which generates `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects pixel dimensions in `WIDTHxHEIGHT` form, not a percentage, so the command fails. The controller ignores the result and repeats the same invalid command five times without reducing the oversized GIF. Calculate pixel dimensions for this branch or use an animation-preserving operation that supports percentage resizing.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: percentage/animated? No—the animated GIF path passes 80% to gifsicle --resize-fit, which requires WxH geometry rather than a percentage, causing resize failure. It also notes the controller ignores the failure and retries the invalid command, matching the golden concern.

false_positives.candidate:
Identify animated GIFs independently of the tempfile suffix

This passes the temporary path rather than the original filename to the optimizer. For an animated GIF backed by an extensionless multipart tempfile, `OptimizedImage.optimize` does not select its animated instructions because it checks whether the input path ends in `.gif`. It instead runs `convert` with the `[0]` frame selector and overwrites the uploaded original with a single frame, even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled. Determine the animation format from the original filename or file contents before resizing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle users without an existing TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never interacted with this topic. For example, this happens when a public-topic email link is forwarded or opened while logged into a different account. TopicView does not establish that a TopicUser row exists, so dereferencing tu.notification_level raises an exception and returns a server error. Treat a missing row as the default notification level and use the create-or-update path when unsubscribing.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, and dereferencing tu.notification_level crashes. The candidate adds the correct handling (default level / create-or-update), which is consistent with the golden issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Protect unsubscribe mutations against CSRF

The new GET endpoints change the logged-in user's notification settings without a signed unsubscribe token. Rails does not require CSRF tokens for GET requests, and this action also bypasses the XHR check. A third-party page can therefore request a predictable URL such as /t/123/unsubscribe.json in an authenticated browser and silently lower or mute that user's notifications. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected request, or validate a recipient-specific unsubscribe token.

Persist unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference

Saving only notification_level leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged. For a user whose reason is nil, an unsubscribe that sets the topic to muted can later be undone by TopicUser.update_last_read: that method automatically assigns tracking whenever the reason is nil and the reading-time threshold is met. Thus reading the topic can unmute an explicitly unsubscribed user. Use TopicUser.change, or otherwise record the user_changed reason and notification-change timestamp along with the new level.

Unsubscribe when the URL is reached through client-side navigation

This route only loads the ordinary topic view; it never invokes the unsubscribe action or changes the notification level. The preference changes only when a full-page request reaches TopicsController#unsubscribe. If the URL is followed through an Ember transition, such as a same-site link while the application is already running, the page displays the unsubscribe confirmation while the user remains subscribed. Ensure the operation is performed for client-side navigation too, rather than relying on the initial HTML request.

Mute watched topics for mailing-list recipients

The new per-topic link is also included in emails generated by mailing_list_notify. However, for a mailing-list user whose topic is watching or tracking, this branch only lowers the level to regular. Regular does not opt a topic out of mailing-list delivery, so subsequent posts keep producing the same emails despite the unsubscribe confirmation. Mailing-list recipients need the topic muted to stop those emails; account for mailing_list_mode when choosing the new level.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
An empty update does not advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt

This call supplies an empty data object to Prisma updateMany. Prisma leaves @updatedAt unchanged when the update payload is empty, so successful cache refreshes never perform the SelectedCalendar timestamp update promised by this new logic. Pass updatedAt explicitly if that metadata should track refreshes, or remove the ineffective call if CalendarCache.updatedAt is the sole intended timestamp.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: an empty Prisma update payload leaves @updatedAt unchanged, so the refresh timestamp is not advanced. The candidate's suggested fix (pass updatedAt explicitly) matches the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use an in-place edit compatible with GNU sed

The existing-variable branch uses BSD-specific sed -i '' syntax. With GNU sed on Linux, the empty argument becomes the script and the replacement expression is treated as an input filename, producing an error without updating GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. The unchecked failure is followed by a success message, leaving webhook registrations pointed at the previous tunnel. Use portable replacement logic and check that the update succeeded.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same portability bug: BSD-style sed -i '' fails under GNU sed on Linux, so the in-place edit does not update the target. The candidate describes the same root cause and consequence with more detail.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendars after deleting cache data

The deletion success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes its optional onChanged prop and disables window-focus refetching, so callers without a refresh callback retain the old cacheUpdatedAt after deletion. The dropdown consequently continues showing a cache timestamp and deletion action for data that no longer exists. Invalidate the connected-calendars query on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

Resolve the environment file relative to the script

ENV_FILE is resolved against the caller's working directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore creates or modifies .env in the repository's parent directory rather than the repository's environment file. The script reports success, but the application never receives the new webhook URL. Resolve the path relative to BASH_SOURCE instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The working-hours end check uses the slot's start time

Both start and end are calculated from slotStartTime, so the check never verifies that the booking finishes within the host's working hours. For example, a fixed host available 09:00–10:00 passes validation for a 60-minute slot at 09:30 generated by another round-robin host's date override. This permits bookings extending beyond the fixed host's availability; end must be calculated from slotEndTime.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the working-hours end boundary is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so the validation fails to ensure the booking ends within availability.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts

When a slot overlaps a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times. This affects both fixed and round-robin hosts, including personal events. For example, an override allowing 10:00–11:00 makes a 10:00 slot available even when an accepted booking or external calendar event occupies that time. An override should replace working hours, not bypass conflict checks.

Require the entire booking to fit within an override

The override checks reject only disjoint intervals, so any partial overlap is treated as availability. With a fixed-host override of 10:00–11:00, a 60-minute slot generated for another host at 09:30 or 10:30 passes, despite extending outside the fixed host's availability. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes because isAfter excludes equality. Both booking boundaries must be contained in an allowed override interval.

Split working hours cause every slot to be rejected

The new working-hours guard rejects a slot if it is outside any interval on that weekday, rather than accepting it if it is inside an interval. For a normal schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00 UTC, morning slots fail against the afternoon interval and afternoon slots fail against the morning interval. Consequently, personal and team events using lunch-break schedules become unbookable even without date overrides.

Apply overrides according to the host's local calendar date

The override's converted start and the slot are compared by UTC calendar date, but a date override replaces a day in the host's timezone. For a Kolkata fixed host normally available Monday 00:00–01:00, a Monday override of 14:00–15:00 must remove the regular early-morning availability. A slot on Sunday at 19:00 UTC is Monday 00:30 locally, yet this comparison misses the override and allows it through the regular working-hours check. Overrides can also incorrectly suppress availability on the adjacent local day.

Multiple override intervals reject each other's slots

dateOverrides.find searches for any same-day interval that does not overlap the slot. If a host has two override windows, such as 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00, a slot in the first window is rejected by the second, and a slot in the second is rejected by the first. Valid split date overrides therefore produce no availability. The check must accept a slot contained in at least one window, rather than reject it for being outside another window.

Split converted overrides when they cross attendee midnight

The timezone conversion extracts only hours and minutes, discarding any date rollover. A 20:00–23:00 UTC override viewed in UTC+2 becomes startTime 1320 (22:00) and endTime 60 (01:00). buildSlots treats this as an invalid interval because startTime exceeds endTime, so a personal event loses the entire override instead of showing its portions on the two attendee dates. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval at midnight.

Override timezone conversion applies DST correction twice

The new offset uses timezone offsets on the override date, so the resulting minutes already account for that date's DST. buildSlots subsequently adds organizerDSTDiff minus inviteeDSTDiff, which is intended to correct working hours calculated with today's offsets. For example, while New York is on UTC−4, a future January override of 10:00–11:00 New York converts correctly to 15:00–16:00 UTC here, but buildSlots shifts it again to 16:00–17:00. Override slots need to avoid that additional correction.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment retry counts atomically to avoid losing failed attempts

Both failure paths assign reminder.retryCount + 1 using the snapshot fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations overlap and both read retryCount=0, their failed scheduling attempts both write 1. Two failures therefore leave the reminder below the deletion threshold, allowing additional scheduling attempts despite the intended two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than overwriting the counter from the fetched value.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same race condition: retryCount is incremented from a stale fetched snapshot in both failure paths, so concurrent updates can overwrite increments. Both recommend Prisma atomic increment.

false_positives.candidate:
Retry cleanup can delete successfully scheduled reminders

The retry-limit branch does not require scheduled=false. Two overlapping cron invocations can both fetch an unscheduled reminder with retryCount=1: one fails and stores 2, while the other succeeds and marks it scheduled without resetting the counter. The next cron run then deletes this successfully scheduled reminder before its scheduled date. Twilio still has the queued SMS, but its local reference is lost, preventing subsequent cancellation or rescheduling through that reminder. Restrict retry-based cleanup to unscheduled SMS reminders.

Failure bookkeeping can abort the entire reminder batch

The update inside the catch block can itself throw, escaping the per-reminder error handling. For example, another cron invocation can delete a reminder after this invocation fetched it because its date has passed or its retry count reached the limit. Updating that missing row throws, and the catch block attempts to update the same missing row again. The resulting uncaught error stops processing all remaining reminders and returns an error for the whole job. Make failure recording tolerate missing rows and handle bookkeeping errors without terminating the batch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Parenthesize the OR-based authorization predicate before returning it

For team/org scopes with members and no optional filters, authConditions is an unparenthesized `A OR B` expression. Returning it directly makes normal raw-query composition unsafe: `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` becomes `A OR (B AND dateConstraint)`, so the team-booking branch bypasses the date constraint. Placing additional constraints before the fragment instead leaves the personal-booking branch unconstrained. Wrap the returned authorization predicate in parentheses and test composition with an additional WHERE constraint for team/org scopes without optional filters.

This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace omitted refresh tokens with a literal placeholder

This fallback also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller previously merged the response into the stored credentials to retain the existing token. Adding the literal `refresh_token` now overwrites that valid stored token, causing the next direct OAuth refresh to fail. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: when an OAuth refresh response omits refresh_token, the code substitutes the literal string 'refresh_token', overwriting the previously stored valid token and causing subsequent refreshes to fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use actual response fields in the minimum token schema

Calling toString() on these Zod schemas produces the literal property name `[object Object]`; it does not match arbitrary response properties. Both computed keys use that name, so the optional unknown property also overwrites the numeric requirement. Since z.object strips unknown properties, a shared response loses expires_in, expiry_date, and any supplied refresh_token. For example, Zoom subsequently computes its expiry from undefined, while Office365 receives no updated expiry.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: computed keys using z.string().toString() produce invalid property names ('[object Object]') instead of real response fields, so the schema fails to capture expires_in/expiry_date/refresh_token. The candidate elaborates on downstream effects but points to the same root cause.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Persist parsed token data rather than the safe-parse result

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safe-parse result shaped as `{ success: true, data: tokens }`, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the tokens themselves. Passing this result directly as the credential key stores the wrapper instead of the Google credential fields. The next service initialization fails googleCredentialSchema.parse because access_token and the other fields are nested under data. true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safe-parse wrapper, but the code persists that wrapper instead of the parsed token payload, causing later credential parsing to fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

The sharing branch always returns a native Fetch Response, but several callbacks normally return different objects. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read `.data`, while HubSpot reads SDK fields such as `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn` directly. None of these callers deserializes the shared Fetch Response, so sharing produces undefined token fields or throws before refreshing credentials. Parse and adapt the shared response, or update these callers to consume a consistent response contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same return-contract mismatch: the credential-sharing path returns a raw Fetch Response, while Google/Zoho callers expect `.data` and HubSpot expects token fields directly, causing runtime failures unless the response is adapted or callers are updated.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

false_positives.candidate:
Import the Prisma client before updating Salesforce credentials

The new database update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor defines it. This fails type checking and, if checks are skipped, fails at runtime before getClient returns a Salesforce connection. Salesforce event creation, updates, and deletion are therefore broken even when credential sharing is disabled.

Send the credential owner's user ID rather than the credential ID

The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is sent to the parent platform as calcomUserId, but this call supplies the Credential table's primary key. Credential IDs and user IDs are unrelated. Whenever this ID matches another user, the parent is asked to refresh and return that other user's Bigin integration; otherwise the lookup fails. Propagate credential.userId through this refresh path instead.

Use the actual Zoom app slug in delegated refresh requests

The delegated request sends appSlug `zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and `zoom` is the app-store slug. A parent platform using the same slug contract as the credential webhook cannot find this integration under `zoomvideo`, so Zoom refreshes fail whenever sharing is enabled.

Delegate Salesforce refreshes to the configured sync endpoint

This new refresh request always goes directly to Salesforce and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured. Applying the sharing-aware parser afterward does not delegate the refresh. Synced credentials without a local provider refresh token fail here, while credentials containing one are refreshed outside the parent platform rather than through the configured source of truth.

Keep local refresh-token expiry checks out of delegated refreshes

The new delegation is reached only after refreshAccessToken checks the locally stored refresh token and deletes the credential if that token is missing or expired. In sharing mode, the parent owns refreshes and the helper specifies that its response only needs an access token and expiry; the local refresh token can therefore be absent or stale while the parent can still supply a valid access token. This path deletes the synced integration instead of contacting the parent. Perform the provider-only validation inside the direct OAuth fallback.

Accept the token-only sync response in the Webex refresh path

After delegating to the sync endpoint, this adapter still validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. The documented shared response containing only the access token and expiry is rejected as an invalid refresh response. The sharing path needs to consume that response and retain the necessary existing credential metadata rather than require a complete Webex OAuth response.

Preserve absolute expiry dates returned by the sync endpoint

A shared response containing access_token and a future expiry_date reaches code that unconditionally replaces expiry_date with Date.now() plus expires_in, defaulting the missing expires_in to zero. The freshly obtained token is consequently stored as immediately expired, forcing another delegated refresh on every subsequent operation. Handle the shared absolute expiry separately from Microsoft's expires_in duration.

Clear the invalid flag when replacing credentials

Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials invalid after unrecoverable authentication failures. This webhook finds those same records but updates only their key, leaving invalid=true after valid replacement tokens are synchronized. The webhook reports success without restoring the installation's validity. Reset the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials.

Make credential creation idempotent under concurrent webhooks

The findFirst followed by create is not atomic. Two concurrent deliveries for a user's first credential can both observe no record and create separate credentials for the same user and app. Later webhook deliveries update only one arbitrary match, leaving the other credential stale and the database inconsistent with the parent source of truth. Serialize the per-user/app operation or enforce an appropriate idempotency constraint.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await the reminder cancellation writes before returning

The promises returned by both cancellation helpers are discarded, while the previously awaited reminder database deletions have been removed. These helpers now perform the only write that marks a scheduled email cancelled or removes an unscheduled reminder. The handler can therefore return success before those writes commit; a serverless invocation can finish with cancellation work still pending, leaving reminders active. Collect and await the helper promises, including the equivalent changed call sites.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: reminder cancellation helper promises are not awaited, so cancellation writes may not commit and scheduled reminders can remain active. The candidate's call to collect/await those promises matches the golden concern about missing awaits at the relevant call sites.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedules still bypass the deferred cancellation mechanism

handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true for every reschedule, so this branch immediately cancels the SendGrid batch rather than recording it for cron. SendGrid retains these cancellations until the original send dates, so 100 future reschedule cancellations still exhaust the limit that caused this bug. Subsequent POST failures are only logged, and cancelled=true is never persisted for cron to retry. Old reminders can therefore still be delivered after rescheduling.

The candidate frames it via the reschedule caller, but the underlying code defect matches.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel imminent reminders before waiting for cron

Scheduled-email cancellations now only set cancelled=true, even when the send time is close. With the 15-minute cron interval, a reminder due at 12:24 and cancelled at 12:01 after the 12:00 run is not processed until 12:15. It is then inside SendGrid's ten-minute no-cancellation window, although an immediate cancellation would have succeeded. These reminders will still be sent; near-term batches need immediate cancellation rather than unconditional deferral.

Isolate failures and commit each successful cancellation

The entire cancellation loop shares one try/catch, and database deletes are deferred until every SendGrid POST succeeds. Prisma queries are lazy, so if any POST rejects, none of the queued deletes execute and every remaining reminder is skipped. A repeatedly failing batch can keep aborting subsequent runs, while successfully cancelled batches are unnecessarily submitted again. Valid reminders can miss their cancellation windows and be delivered. Handle errors per reminder and execute each successful reminder's delete before moving on.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist

Blacklist entries are lowercased, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. z.string().email() accepts uppercase characters, so a blacklisted address such as blocked@example.com can be invited by submitting BLOCKED@example.com. Normalize submitted addresses before checking BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS so casing cannot bypass the configured exclusion.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same blacklist bypass: blacklist entries are lowercased, but submitted guest emails are compared without normalization, allowing uppercase variants to evade BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Deduplicate guest addresses on the server

uniqueGuests only filters addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted array. The server schema also accepts duplicates, so a request containing the same new address twice passes both values to createMany, creating duplicate attendees and sending duplicate invitation emails. The dialog's client-side Set validation does not protect the mutation from direct requests. Enforce uniqueness server-side before inserting guests.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify that uniqueGuests only excludes existing attendees and does not deduplicate repeated emails within the submitted array, allowing createMany to insert duplicate attendee rows. The candidate's extra details do not change the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Honor disabled standard-email settings for guest additions

sendAddGuestsEmails sends host and attendee emails unconditionally and has no event-type metadata parameter. Unlike the scheduled and location-change email helpers, it never checks disableStandardEmails.all.host or disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest consequently sends notifications to recipients whose standard emails were explicitly disabled, including existing attendees, and can duplicate replacement workflow emails. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the existing email-disable checks.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: sendAddGuestsEmails sends host/attendee emails without checking EventType disableStandardEmails flags, so notifications go out even when standard emails are disabled.

false_positives.candidate:
Use the booking organizer's credentials to update the calendar

The authorization check permits attendees and team admins to add guests, but EventManager is constructed with the caller's credentials. For a logged-in attendee with no connected calendar, those credentials cannot update the organizer's existing calendar references. The new guests are saved to the booking, but the organizer's Google/Outlook event remains unchanged. Construct the manager with the booking organizer and their credentials instead.

Authorize either team admins or team owners

The team authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. A team admin who is not the owner therefore fails this check and receives FORBIDDEN when adding guests to another member's booking, unless they are also an attendee. Use || so either privileged team role grants access.

Validate booking status before sending confirmed invitations

After finding the booking, the handler checks authorization but never checks its status. An organizer or attendee can therefore add guests to a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or PENDING booking. The subsequent guest-update emails attach an ICS with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, sending confirmed invitations for an event whose stored status remains cancelled, rejected, or pending. Reject unsupported booking states before creating attendees or use a status-appropriate notification flow.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Consume backup codes atomically

Backup-code validation reads the encrypted array from the earlier user query, then replaces the entire array with an unconditional update by user ID. Two concurrent requests can both validate and authenticate with the same supposedly single-use code. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a consumed code. Validation and consumption need an atomic conditional update or a transaction that locks the row before reading and checking the codes.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the non-atomic read-modify-write of backup codes, allowing concurrent requests to reuse the same single-use code. The candidate adds a related overwrite race, but the core issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code authentication can bypass password verification

Password verification for CAL accounts is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. The new backup-code branch then authenticates without validating that TOTP value. A request containing an email, a valid backup code, an arbitrary totpCode such as "x", and an incorrect or empty password therefore succeeds. Require verified first-factor authentication before accepting the backup code; an unvalidated TOTP field must not exempt the request from password verification.

Backup recovery is unavailable in the external-provider 2FA flow

The new Lost access button is rendered only through TwoFactorFooter, while logins with totpEmail use ExternalTotpFooter, which contains only Cancel. A user who generates backup codes as a CAL account and later links Google or SAML retains those codes, but cannot reach the backup-code input after signing in through that provider. Posting a backup code without a TOTP code is also rejected by the external-provider guards in authorize. Wire backup recovery into the external-provider verification flow so these users can recover without their authenticator.

Notify the caller when 2FA has actually been enabled

After the enable endpoint succeeds, onEnable is now deferred until the custom backup-codes Close button is clicked. Dismissing the dialog through its normal onOpenChange path, such as Escape, never invokes onEnable even though 2FA is already enabled on the server. This breaks the callback contract and leaves callers relying on it uninformed about the successful change. Ensure every dismissal after successful enablement propagates that result, or synchronize the enabled state independently of closing the backup-code screen.

Wait for clipboard success before confirming the codes were copied

navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise that can reject, for example when clipboard access is denied. This handler does not await or catch it and immediately displays "Backup codes copied!" regardless of the outcome. Users can close the backup-code screen believing they copied their recovery credentials when the clipboard was never updated. Show success only after the write resolves and report copying failures.

Adding tabIndex={-1} to the shared PasswordField visibility button removes it from the keyboard focus order everywhere this component is used. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach and activate Show password or Hide password with Tab and Enter/Space, although the control remains available to mouse users. Keep this interactive control in the tab order.

Do not override PasswordField's visibility-controlled input type

The replacement PasswordField still receives type="password". PasswordField spreads its props after setting the input type from its visibility state, so this explicit prop overrides the computed "text" type. Clicking the new Show password control changes its icon but never reveals the password. Remove the explicit type prop here or prevent it from overriding PasswordField's internal visibility state.
